why.text: Hot, dry summers ripen Pedro Ximénez quickly. The Superior subzone is planted on albariza soils.

styles.text: Dry to sweet whites, young or aged; fortified fino, amontillado and oloroso; sweet Pedro Ximénez and Moscatel.

climate.text: Semi-continental Mediterranean: long, hot, dry summers and short, relatively mild winters, which speed up ripening.

soil.text: The Superior subzone covers albariza soils.

tastes.text: Whites: pale yellow to golden, dry to sweet, light, with Pedro Ximénez character. Fino: straw to gold, dry, flor-aged. Oloroso: mahogany, full and velvety. Pedro Ximénez: amber to deep mahogany, dense, raisined, sweet.

styles.name: Fino
styles.text: Straw to gold, dry, biological ageing, slightly bitter, light and fragrant.

styles.name: Amontillado
styles.text: Amber to old gold, pungent, nutty, dry or nearly off-dry.

styles.name: Oloroso
styles.text: Mahogany, aromatic, dry or slightly off-dry, full and velvety.

styles.name: Pedro Ximénez
styles.text: Sweet liqueur wine, amber to deep mahogany, dense, raisined notes.

why.text: Half the area lies above 1,000 m. Big day-night swings and poor, limy soil shape the wines.

styles.text: White, rosado and red wines, plus sparkling wines and sweet wines from overripe grapes.

climate.text: Large day-night swings; absolute highs of 39 °C and lows of -4 °C; 450 mm of rain a year over about 70 rainy days.

soil.text: Brown limy soil, poor in organic matter, phosphorus and nitrogen.

altitude.text: Half of the area lies above 1,000 m above sea level.

tastes.text: Reds: bright cherry to deep red; red berries; full body, high astringency. Whites: greenish yellow to straw; fruity, intense aromas. Rosés: pale pink to light red; medium to intense fruit.

styles.name: Vino de uvas sobremaduradas
styles.text: White, rosé or red wine made from overripe grapes.

styles.name: Vino espumoso de calidad
styles.text: White, rosé or red sparkling wine with persistent foam.

why.text: A flat Guadalquivir lowland near Doñana, where Atlantic influence softens a Mediterranean climate. Many wines age in solera.

styles.text: Whites and reds, young to aged; fortified generosos and sweet liqueur wines, including mistelas.

climate.text: Mediterranean with Atlantic touches; flat to gently rolling land in the Guadalquivir depression, next to Doñana National Park.

tastes.text: Whites: bright pale straw with green tints to deeper yellow; fresh fruit and wild herbs; light yet intense. Reds: cherry with garnet rims; powerful, elegant aromas; tasty, concentrated.

styles.name: Condado Viejo
styles.text: Liqueur wine from white varieties, amber to mahogany, toasted almond aroma.

styles.name: Generoso
styles.text: Dry, aged biologically or oxidatively; pale yellow to dark mahogany, nutty.

styles.name: Mistela
styles.text: Dark liqueur wine with macerated fruit aromas, creamy on the palate.

styles.name: Gran Reserva
styles.text: Red with dark cherry colour, mineral and complex aroma; fleshy and powerful.

why.text: Mountains and sea temper a strong Mediterranean sun that gives high natural alcohol. The sun also lets growers dry grapes for sweet wines.

styles.text: Dry whites; dry and sweet liqueur wines; sweet wines from sun-dried or overripe grapes.

climate.text: Mediterranean with very high sunshine, shaped by mountain relief, the nearby sea and an Atlantic transition.

tastes.text: Dry white: yellow to amber, penetrating, powerful aroma. Liqueur wines: intense nose, integrated alcohol; sweet ones unctuous and persistent. Raisined-grape wines: pale yellow to old gold; concentrated, acid-sweet balance.

styles.name: Dulce Natural
styles.text: Sweet liqueur wine showing varietal, fermentation and fortification aromas.

styles.name: Vino de uvas pasificadas
styles.text: Sweet wine from raisined grapes, pale yellow to old gold, very unctuous.

styles.name: Vino Naturalmente Dulce
styles.text: Sweet overripe-grape wine, fresh, lively, unctuous and persistent.

why.text: Europe's southernmost sierras sit close to the sea, with cool nights and well-drained soil. Ripening is very sunny but moderate.

styles.text: Whites, rosados and reds, from fresh young wines to oak-aged ones.

climate.text: Singular Mediterranean: very high sunshine, moderate ripening temperatures and cool nights, shaped by relief and sea.

soil.text: Well-drained soils of medium to low fertility.

tastes.text: Reds: violet-red to ruby, tile tones with ageing; fruity, earthy; structured, ripe tannins. Whites: straw with green glints to gold; fruity, fresh when young, unctuous in oak. Rosés: pink to reddish, fruity, floral.

why.text: Flat farmland lies beside the Guadalquivir marshes. A long, hard summer topping 40 °C shapes a traditional style.

styles.text: Young whites; reds from young to gran reserva; flor-aged generosos; liqueur and natural sweet wines; mistela.

climate.text: Mild autumn and spring; long, harsh summer with highs that can pass 40 °C, August hottest; almost all land is flat.

tastes.text: Reds: bright ruby to deep cherry; ripe fruit, vanilla and coffee when oaked; fleshy, full-bodied, velvety. Whites: very pale, fruity, dry or off-dry. Flor de Lebrija: straw yellow, almond, dry.

styles.name: Flor de Lebrija
styles.text: Dry generoso aged under flor; straw yellow, almond aroma, light on the palate.

styles.name: Lebrija Old Vino Seco
styles.text: Generoso in amber to mahogany, with a walnut aroma.

styles.name: Lebrija Old Dulce
styles.text: Generoso de licor, amber to dark mahogany, full-bodied, pungent, muted aroma.

styles.name: Dulce natural
styles.text: Gold to mahogany; honey, caramel and raisin aromas; velvety, glyceric.

why.text: Vines suited to the climate grow on albariza, a soft marl that holds moisture. Flor yeast and soleras age the wines.

styles.text: Dry generosos (fino, amontillado, oloroso, palo cortado); sweet Moscatel and Pedro Ximénez; sweetened liqueur types.

soil.text: Albarizas: soft marls that hold moisture well.

styles.name: Fino, Amontillado, Oloroso, Palo Cortado
styles.text: Vino Generoso type, dry: no more than 5 g/l reducing sugars.

why.text: Sea air and high humidity feed an intense, lasting layer of flor yeast. That flor gives Manzanilla its character.

styles.text: Pale straw to pale gold generoso wine, aged wholly under flor yeast in Sanlúcar de Barrameda.

climate.text: Sea nearby and high humidity favour intense, lasting activity of the flor yeast.

tastes.text: Pale gold to straw yellow; aroma and flavour of biological ageing under flor.

styles.name: Manzanilla
styles.text: Generoso aged wholly under flor, only in Sanlúcar de Barrameda cellars.
